description: Make AgentSession follow-up a real continuation: persist stable SessionInput/AgentTurn subrecords with idempotent identity, decouple acceptance from delivery, and expose a three-valued call contract shared by Web and CLI.

tasks.title: Server grain: follow-up input & turn lifecycle
tasks.description: The AgentSession grain's follow-up accept transition persists an AgentSessionInputRecord (stable Id, sequence, text, source, Acceptance=Accepted, no JobId, stored idempotency key) and assigns it to an AgentTurnRecord per the turn-assignment rule (idle/queued-turn joins; executing-turn starts a new queued turn). Retrying with the same idempotency key resolves to the same input with no duplicate. Runtime events progress follow-up turn status: a session.input event correlated by operationId marks the linked turn Executing; a session.activity idle event marks it terminal. The AgentSessionFollowupLease gains InputId/TurnId so operationId resolves to the turn. Omitted idempotency keys are minted unique per call (recovery convention).
acceptanceCriteria: Accepting a follow-up persists an AgentSessionInputRecord with a stable Id, next sequence, submitted text, source, Acceptance=Accepted, and no JobId, before the accept transition returns.
Retrying a follow-up with the same idempotency key returns the same Input Id and creates no second SessionInput; a different key creates a distinct input.
An omitted idempotency key is minted unique per call, so omission is not retry-idempotent.

A follow-up accepted while idle or while a turn is queued joins that turn's InputIds in order; a follow-up accepted while a turn is executing creates a new queued turn and does not interrupt or merge into the executing turn.

A session.input runtime event carrying a follow-up operationId marks the linked AgentTurn Executing; a session.activity idle event carrying that operationId marks it terminal (completed/failed/unknown).
An accepted SessionInput and its AgentTurn survive a grain state reload with the same Ids, sequence, and status.
When the session input queue is at capacity, new follow-ups are rejected and previously accepted inputs remain unchanged.
Server domain/grain unit and spec tests pass with fakes (no real runtime/network/wall-clock), covering acceptance, idempotent retry, turn assignment, status progression, and restart durability.
tasks.output: AgentSession grain follow-up accept transition and runtime-event turn-progression hooks with passing server tests
tasks.notes: Mirrors the launch path's EnsureInitialLaunch/MarkInitialTurnExecuting/MarkInitialTurnTerminal for follow-up inputs. No runner change is needed for correlation — the runner continues emitting operationId-correlated session.input/session.activity events; the lease carries InputId/TurnId for server-side resolution.

tasks.title: Server API: three-valued follow-up call contract and observation surface
tasks.description: The follow-up HTTP routes (canonical and issue-scoped alias) read the Idempotency-Key header, call the grain's accept transition, and return a three-valued result (accepted/rejected/unknown) with the stable inputId and turnId on accepted. Acceptance is decoupled from delivery: accepted is returned once the input is persisted, regardless of runner dispatch outcome; a runner-offline result no longer reverts acceptance. The session summary DTO is extended to expose follow-up SessionInput acceptance and AgentTurn status so clients can distinguish accepted-pending from executing.
acceptanceCriteria: POST followup returns status accepted with inputId and turnId once the SessionInput is persisted, even when the runner is offline or unavailable (input accepted-and-queued).
POST followup returns rejected for confirmed non-acceptance (empty text, session not found, recovery in progress, capacity exceeded) without creating a SessionInput.
POST followup returns unknown when the server cannot confirm persistence (grain timeout/lost response), directing the caller to reconcile with the same call identity.
Both the canonical /agent-sessions/{id}/followup route and the issue-scoped alias return the same result shape.
The Idempotency-Key header is read and forwarded to the grain; a retry with the same key returns the original inputId/turnId.
The session summary/observation DTO exposes follow-up inputs (with acceptance) and turns (with status), sufficient to distinguish accepted-pending (queued) from executing.
Server API tests pass (fake grain/runner), covering the three outcomes, idempotency-key forwarding, decoupled acceptance, and the observation DTO.
tasks.output: Updated AgentSessionFollowupRoutes, issue-scoped alias, and session observation DTO with passing server API tests
tasks.notes: Replaces the binary AgentSessionFollowupResult(SessionId, "sent") with the three-valued status plus inputId/turnId. The result shape change has no compatibility shim (active development, no version compat).

tasks.title: Web: follow-up idempotency key and accepted-pending vs executing status
tasks.description: The Web follow-up flow generates and sends an Idempotency-Key header per submission and reuses it on retry. The composer and session view render follow-up status using the shared model: accepted/rejected/unknown outcome, input acceptance, and turn status (queued vs executing), distinguishing accepted-pending from executing.
acceptanceCriteria: useFollowupMutation / postFollowup send an Idempotency-Key header generated per submission and reuse the same key on a retry after a lost response.
The follow-up composer and session view render accepted-pending (queued turn) distinctly from executing, derived from the observation DTO input acceptance and turn status.
Web typecheck (npm run typecheck -w packages/web) and tests (npm run test:run -w packages/web) pass.
tasks.output: Updated Web followup mutation, API client, and composer/session view with passing typecheck and tests
tasks.notes: Consumes the new API result shape and observation DTO from T-002.

tasks.title: CLI: follow-up idempotency key and status output
tasks.description: The mo session followup command sends an Idempotency-Key (generated per invocation, reusable on retry) and surfaces the three-valued outcome with inputId, turnId, and the accepted-pending vs executing status, using the same interpretation as Web.
acceptanceCriteria: mo session followup sends an Idempotency-Key header and reuses it on retry.
The command output surfaces the accepted/rejected/unknown outcome and the inputId/turnId, and distinguishes accepted-pending from executing using the same status model as Web.
CLI tests (packages/cli) pass, covering idempotency-key sending, the new result fields, and the issue-scoped/canonical routes.
tasks.output: Updated mo session followup command and output with passing CLI tests
tasks.notes: Independent of T-003 (Web); both consume the shared API contract from T-002.
